jurisdiction.name: Italy
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Italy was the first EU country to adopt a general national AI law: Law 132/2025, in force since 10 October 2025, sets principles for AI use across sectors, creates a deepfake offence, and names the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as national AI authorities. Two 2026 legislative decrees under that law cover police use of AI and liability, and the EU AI Act's authorities, fines, sandbox and training, with AI clauses also in the public contracts code and the workplace transparency decree. National policy rests on the 2024-2026 AI strategy (replacing the 2022-2024 programme) and AgID's three-year IT plan for public administration, with draft AgID guidelines on adopting, buying and developing AI in the public sector and ministry documents on AI at work, in schools and in defence. The data protection authority (Garante) is among the most active AI enforcers in Europe, with orders and fines against ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Replika, Clearview AI, Character.AI and delivery platforms' algorithms, while the competition authority, the communications regulator, the Bank of Italy and IVASS have added AI decisions and communications.
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 11 October 2026 and covers national law, the national government and ministries, and regulators. Regional and city documents were not reviewed, in line with the project's rule for Italy. European Union and Council of Europe instruments are shown through the regional files. The decree implementing the EU AI Act enters into force on 23 October 2026, so it is shown as published but not yet in force. The data protection authority's 2024 fine on OpenAI was annulled by a court in 2026 and is shown as repealed. Four documents could only be located because their websites blocked access.

It sets strategic actions in four macro-areas (research, public administration, businesses, training) plus cross-cutting actions such as a national registry of AI datasets and models, network infrastructure for AI and a Foundation for AI to manage implementation, coordination and monitoring. It includes a monitoring system with quantitative indicators and a chapter on the regulatory context and the authorities needed to supervise the EU AI Act nationally.

instruments.issuing_authority: Parliament (Camera dei deputati and Senato della Repubblica); promulgated by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: In force since 10 October 2025 (GU Serie Generale n. 223 of 25 September 2025). Amended: rectification notice of 17 October 2025 (art. 26(1)(a)); D.L. 31 ottobre 2025, n. 159 (art. 14(7), converted by L. 29 dicembre 2025, n. 198) added the Minister of Labour to the art. 19(6) coordination committee; D.L. 26 giugno 2026, n. 107 (art. 14(1)) added art. 24(5-bis), allowing up to EUR 100 million from the 'PN scuola 2021-2027' programme for AI literacy and training measures. The delegations of arts. 16 and 24 were exercised by D.Lgs. 9 settembre 2026, n. 160 and D.Lgs. 7 ottobre 2026, n. 179 (Normattiva 'atti correlati', checked 2026-10-11).
instruments.scope: Research, testing, development, adoption and use of AI systems and models in Italy; to be interpreted and applied consistently with Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
instruments.summary: Italy's framework AI law (28 articles) sets human-centric principles for AI, requires parental consent for children under 14 to access AI and allows 14-17-year-olds to consent themselves, and adds sector rules for health, work (employers must inform workers of AI use), intellectual professions (AI only as support, with disclosure to clients), public administration (AI only supports decisions, with the official keeping responsibility) and justice. Article 20 designates the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) as AI notifying authority and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as market surveillance authority and single point of contact under the EU AI Act, without prejudice to the Bank of Italy, CONSOB and IVASS; article 19 sets the national AI strategy process and a coordination committee, and article 23 authorises up to EUR 1 billion of equity investment in AI, cybersecurity and quantum companies. It protects only human-authored works under copyright law (art. 25), creates the offence of unlawful dissemination of AI-generated or altered content (deepfakes, art. 612-quater c.p., 1-5 years) and an aggravating circumstance for crimes committed with AI (art. 26), and delegates the Government to adapt national law to the AI Act and regulate unlawful AI uses within 12 months (arts. 16 and 24).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Italy's horizontal national AI law; designates the national AI Act authorities (AgID, ACN) and is the legal basis for the implementing legislative decrees.

instruments.english_title: Legislative Decree No. 160 of 9 September 2026 - Adapting national law to Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) on the use of AI systems for police activities and on civil and criminal liability
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Italy (Council of Ministers); issued by the President of the Republic
instruments.current_status: Published in GU Serie Generale n. 214 of 15 September 2026; in force 30 September 2026. Adopted under the delegation in art. 24(3)-(5) of Law 132/2025 (scheme approved preliminarily by the Council of Ministers on 10 June 2026 - Atto del Governo n. 418 - and finally on 4 August 2026, after opinions of the Garante, the Conferenza unificata (20 July 2026) and the parliamentary committees, as recited in the preamble). Police AI systems already in use must be made compliant within one year (art. 21).
instruments.scope: Use of AI systems by Italian police forces; criminal offences and corporate liability involving AI; civil damages actions for harm caused by AI systems
instruments.summary: Regulates the research, testing, training and use of AI systems by the police forces, including biometric categorisation, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces only for the AI Act's permitted purposes (with a new art. 359-ter c.p.p.), fundamental-rights impact assessments, logging and retrospective facial recognition. It creates the offence of failing to adopt security or human-oversight measures for high-risk AI systems, or unlawfully altering them (art. 437-bis c.p.), and makes companies liable under D.Lgs. 231/2001 for that offence and for deepfake dissemination (art. 612-quater c.p.). For civil claims it provides access to evidence, a rebuttable presumption of causation where harm follows a breach of the AI Act, says AI Act conformity does not by itself exclude liability, and gives a right to ask about the defendant's liability insurance.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First implementing decree of Law 132/2025; national rules on police use of AI and on criminal and civil liability for AI systems.

instruments.scope: Operators within the scope of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (art. 2(1)); national AI authorities and market surveillance authorities; schools, universities, professions, employers, health and public administration for AI training measures
instruments.summary: Italy's AI Act implementing decree: confirms AgID as notifying authority and ACN as market surveillance authority and single point of contact, makes the Bank of Italy, CONSOB and IVASS market surveillance authorities for high-risk AI in banking, investment and insurance services and the Garante for the cases in AI Act art. 74(8), and sets their supervisory, inspection, registration (ACN for Annex III point 2 systems) and sanctioning powers. It sets administrative fines of up to EUR 35 million or 7% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices and up to EUR 15 million or 3% for other breaches, and establishes the Italian AI regulatory sandbox under AI Act art. 57 run by AgID and ACN. Chapter III adds AI training measures for students, teachers, adults, public employees, justice staff, professionals and health workers, requires that final employment decisions taken with AI be made by a person, and protects AI training data, algorithms and methods as trade secrets (art. 98(1-bis) of the industrial property code).
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main national AI Act implementing act: designates and empowers the authorities, sets the penalty regime and creates the national AI sandbox.

instruments.scope: Contracting authorities and awarding entities (stazioni appaltanti and enti concedenti); AI-relevant provision is art. 30
instruments.summary: Italy's public procurement code; article 30 tells contracting authorities to automate their activities where possible, including with artificial intelligence and distributed-ledger technologies. When buying or developing such solutions they must secure the source code and documentation needed to understand how they work and include maintenance clauses to correct errors. Automated decisions must respect knowability and comprehensibility, non-exclusivity of the algorithmic decision (meaningful human control) and algorithmic non-discrimination, and public administrations must publish the list of the technological solutions they use in the 'Amministrazione trasparente' section of their websites.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions for public procurement and automated decisions by contracting authorities.

instruments.scope: Public and private employers and principals (committenti) using automated decision-making or monitoring systems
instruments.summary: Italy's 'Decreto Trasparenza' transposes the EU directive on transparent and predictable working conditions; its article 4 adds article 1-bis to D.Lgs. 152/1997, requiring employers to inform workers before work starts when automated decision-making or monitoring systems are used for hiring, management, termination, task assignment, monitoring or evaluation. Employers must explain the aspects affected, the purposes, logic and functioning of the systems, the data categories and main parameters used to train them, control and correction measures, and their accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity metrics, and workers or their unions may request further information.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Labour-law transparency duties for algorithmic management, cross-referenced by art. 11 of Law 132/2025 as the vehicle for informing workers of AI use.
